verdict: Palo Alto Networks grew revenue 15% to $2.59B and earned $432M — a clean, profitable quarter before the CyberArk and Chronosphere deals closed and reshaped the next one.

segments.name: Subscription & support
segments.note: Security subscriptions and support — the recurring core of the business.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling security platforms to enterprises — the largest running cost.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

otherDetail: Other income, net of $152M, with no interest expense in the quarter.
oneTimers: Share-based compensation was $321M, acquisition-related costs $24M and amortization of acquired intangible assets $38M — together they explain most of the gap between the $432M GAAP net income and $732M of non-GAAP net income.
The Chronosphere and CyberArk acquisitions closed just after this quarter ended, in early February 2026 — their revenue and costs first appear in Q3 FY26.
footerNote: Palo Alto guided Q3 FY26 revenue to $2.941B–$2.945B in this release.

takeaways.title: Steady growth
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 15% to $2.59B — product revenue rose 22% to $514M and subscription and support 13% to $2.08B.

takeaways.title: The platform bet is working
takeaways.text: Next-Generation Security ARR grew 33% to $6.3B, and remaining performance obligations rose 23% to $16.0B.

takeaways.title: Profitably run
takeaways.text: GAAP net income rose to $432M from $267M a year ago, with operating income up to $397M — the last clean quarter before two big acquisitions landed.
